problem: Neighbors and small community groups want to organize informal sports pickup games (e.g., basketball, soccer, badminton) but lack a simple tool to propose a game, collect RSVPs, set a time, and manage last‑minute changes, leading to low turnout and wasted effort.
solution: PickupPlay is a lightweight, offline‑first web app that lets a host create a game event, specify sport, location, date, and time, and share a short link. Participants can RSVP, add comments, and the host can see a real‑time attendee list. All data is stored locally in the browser, so no backend is required.
target_customers: urban residents who play informal sports

competitors.name: Meetup
competitors.difference: Meetup is a broad social platform with paid plans and requires an account; PickupPlay is free, no login, focused on quick sports games.

competitors.name: TeamSnap
competitors.difference: TeamSnap targets organized teams and charges per season; PickupPlay is for ad‑hoc games with zero cost.

features: Create game event with sport, location, date, time

monetization.pricing_hypothesis: Offer a premium add‑on that lets hosts export attendee lists as CSV and remove the branding after a $2.99 one‑time purchase.
monetization.free_tier: All core features remain free; premium is optional.

operating_costs: Current prototype: ₹0 within published free‑tier limits
launch_strategy: Publish repo on GitHub, enable GitHub Pages, share the link in local park community groups and on neighborhood subreddits.
Gather feedback from 5‑10 users and iterate.

marketing_content.tagline: Turn a casual invite into a full‑court game.
marketing_content.social_post: 🚀 Introducing PickupPlay – the fastest way to set up a basketball, soccer, or badminton game with your neighbors. No login, no fees, just a link and a game. Try it now and get the ball rolling! #CommunitySports #FreeApp

tests: Create a new game, copy the link, open it in a second browser tab, RSVP as a participant, and verify the host view shows the name.
Refresh the page and ensure the event persists via localStorage.
next_improvements: Add optional email reminders (via mailto links)
Allow multiple concurrent events per user
